claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain and toughness than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
The enhanced plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr are primarily caused by synergistic lattice distortions induced by chemical complexity.
Lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr generate heterogeneous local stress fields.
The heterogeneous local stress fields activate additional or diverse slip systems.
The heterogeneous local stress fields encourage dislocation cross-slip and pinning.
Cross-slip and dislocation pinning increase strain hardening and delay brittle fracture.
The equimolar multi-principal-element composition of WTaTiVZr produces significant lattice distortion.
Cross-slip and pinning provide enhanced dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr.
The proposed dislocation behavior delays the transition to brittle failure relative to pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, WTaTiVZr will begin plastic deformation earlier than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, WTaTiVZr will have a higher strain-hardening rate than pure tungsten.
TEM will reveal greater dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
TEM will reveal cross-slip and possibly twinning in WTaTiVZr under high-temperature loading.
The proposed mechanism is applicable in high-temperature regimes and at controlled strain rates relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
The results may differ outside the specified thermal and loading conditions.
Matching grain size, texture, defect structure, processing history, strain rate, and thermal cycling would make composition the intended controlled difference between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
